clue.text: Froth seeing somewhat crazy second bed

parts.note: cuckoo is an informal word for a bit mad
pit is slang for one's bed

explanation.surface: Someone sees a bed that is only a little crazy, beside a foamy mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuckoo spit is the frothy blob a froghopper nymph leaves on plant stems.
explanation.definitionFit: The name describes the foamy secretion made by spittlebug larvae on garden plants.

clue.text: Sniffles caught by elderly

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
elderly means old

explanation.surface: An old person comes down with a case of the sniffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sniffles are the typical symptom of a common viral infection of the nose, used here for the illness itself.

clue.text: Vehicle, very close to aggressive and amiss, to swerve thus

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of aggressive, taken at its close
something amiss is up, as in 'what's up?'

explanation.surface: A car comes up very close to an aggressive driver and something goes wrong as it swerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints the scene; the definition is the closing phrase, describing the manoeuvre the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve someone up is to overtake and cut sharply in front of another vehicle, a dangerous swerve.

clue.text: Clichéd start in a poem — continue working

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, i.e. reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet is told to keep working on a poem that opens with a cliché.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock opening of fairy tales, the most hackneyed way to begin a story.

clue.text: Nursery worker's flapping made sense for the most part

indicators.note: flapping suggests letters thrown into a flurry and rearranged
most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A gardener at a plant nursery got flustered but mostly talked sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery is for plants, not children.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedsman sells or raises seeds, the kind of person who works in a plant nursery.

clue.text: Name dropped in explosive prefatory matter

indicators.note: dropped means let fall from its place at the head of the word
the dropped letter lands inside the word again, one slot lower

parts.note: nitro is short for nitroglycerine, an explosive

explanation.surface: A name gets dropped into an explosive preface.
explanation.walkthrough: The N at the front of the explosive slips one place down, swapping with the I.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening material that comes before the main text or music.

clue.text: Knight of the Garter embraced by monarch

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside, so the word goes within

parts.note: KG is the post-nominal letters of a Knight of the Garter
by and in can both mean during or by way of, as in 'by night'/'in the night'

explanation.surface: A knight of the Garter is hugged by the sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: KG are the letters a Knight of the Order of the Garter, Britain's senior order of chivalry, puts after their name.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is a male sovereign ruler, a straightforward synonym of monarch.

clue.text: Conceive fancy peace song?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to form an idea in the mind
second meaning: to suppose or picture
third meaning: John Lennon's 1971 song about a world at peace

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions in a row; the question mark covers the song being an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to form a mental picture, and it is also the title of Lennon's famous anthem for world harmony.

clue.text: Visitor I finally defeat is to reckon without specific thought

parts.note: a guest is a visitor
mate in chess is the final defeat of the king

explanation.surface: A guest finally beats someone, and the result is reckoned roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To guesstimate is to make a rough estimate from intuition rather than careful calculation.

clue.text: A part of unusually rich poem

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is taken, the letters spanning the gap

parts.note: the poem spans the end of unusually and most of rich

explanation.surface: A section of an unusually rich poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem expressing personal feeling, or the words of a song.

clue.text: Exciting ten days for us followers?

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: our means belonging to us
days, as in 'in my day', means an age or era

explanation.surface: Ten thrilling days spent by a band of devotees.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants or hangers-on accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Powerless to grasp snub of utterly absorbing read

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing such a read

indicators.note: grasping means holding something within

parts.note: powerless means unable
a put-down is a snub

explanation.surface: Someone is powerless to grasp the slight in a gripping book.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that is unputdownable is so gripping and compelling that the reader cannot stop.

clue.text: Coat with this material is not commonly worn on impulse at the front

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go before the next piece
worn suggests something battered out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of is not

explanation.surface: A coat that is not usually worn on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' looks like a garment worn on impulse; it is a coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion paint is the water-based decorating paint used to put a coat on walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Refuse when recycled appears wet

indicators.note: recycling turns material into something new, so these letters are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: Rubbish looks soggy once it has been recycled.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste paper is discarded paper, a kind of rubbish that is commonly recycled.

clue.text: OK, apparently cricket ground welcomes runs

indicators.note: the ground greets runs at its door, so that letter stands right before it

parts.note: app. is the dictionary abbreviation for apparently
the Oval is a London cricket ground

explanation.surface: A cricket ground seemingly gives its blessing as runs pile up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a Test cricket ground in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving the OK to something is giving it your approval or sanction.

clue.text: Master flying jet

indicators.note: letters sent flying land in a new order

explanation.surface: A master is flying a jet aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' looks like an aircraft; it is a gush of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet of water is a narrow forceful flow, the same as a stream.

clue.text: Firm's do supported by island

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: to do someone is to con them
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A company's party is backed by a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company; it is the adjective meaning solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete means solid and definite, as in concrete evidence or a firm proposal.

clue.text: Near fine upper class

parts.note: to can mean near or close, as when a door is pulled to
phat is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Nearly good enough for the posh set.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-hat as an adjective means belonging to the wealthy elite, after the tall silk hat of the gentry.

clue.text: Eat before appointment

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
a date is an appointment

explanation.surface: Have a bite before a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Predate' usually means come earlier, but it is also the back-formation from predator: to prey on.
explanation.definitionFit: To predate is to hunt and devour prey, so eating is what a predator does.

clue.text: Chauffeur maybe found by old hill shrouded in haze

indicators.note: a shroud wraps around, so the words go inside

parts.note: mist is a haze
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A chauffeur is discovered near an ancient hill wreathed in mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur is one example of a driver of a car, which is what a motorist is.

clue.text: Unfortunately I retain an inclination to indolence

indicators.note: things going badly signals the letters going awry into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sadly admits to a tendency to laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness, a reluctance to move or act.

clue.text: Leave behind US author with Twitch's flexing of literal facts

indicators.note: the first word goes after the pieces that follow it

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American author
a tic is a twitch
licence can mean leave or permission

explanation.surface: An American writer with a twitch bends the facts in his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic licence is the freedom an artist takes to depart from fact or rules for effect.

clue.text: Wood that forms the braces of William Tell's bow

parts.note: a brace is a pair, and this letter appears doubled in both names
to bow is to bend in a curve, to arch

explanation.surface: The timber from which William Tell's crossbow was made.
explanation.walkthrough: William and Tell each hold a pair of one letter, so 'braces' means pairs, not supports.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch is a conifer whose tough timber is used in building and boatmaking.

clue.text: Vocally opposed to advanced payment

indicators.note: spoken out loud, one word passes for another

parts.note: anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: Someone loudly objects to being paid up front.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake a poker player puts in before the cards are dealt.

clue.text: Growing feature of avenue? Earth perhaps and endless grass

parts.note: Earth is an example of a planet

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: An avenue's leafy feature grows from earth and a bit of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth' reads as soil for growing; it is the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The London plane is the classic street tree lining city avenues, so it is a living part of the scene.

clue.text: Marching staff keep playing

parts.note: batting is playing, in cricket
on means continuing, as in 'keep on'

explanation.surface: A band's marching staff are told to keep playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 3,2 the answer means to carry on batting in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is the stick twirled by the leader of a marching band.

clue.text: Bank reversed charge, right

indicators.note: the pieces are written backwards

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: A bank cancels a charge, and rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money; it is a ridge in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or coral near the water's surface, an underwater bank.

clue.text: Tart's imagery focusing on appeal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sweet baked dessert, here one with a soft cheese filling
second meaning: photographs of attractive women posed for sex appeal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' leans towards the slang for a woman, which chimes with the second, pin-up sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a creamy dessert on a biscuit base and glamour photography of scantily clad models.
